title: Plan K: AI Meeting Notes Workflow
summary: Record & transcribe → AI summary → extract action items → archive & distribute → follow up & review
scenario: Best for regular meetings, client calls, brainstorming and interviews — turning 'meetings you had' into executable knowledge assets.

steps.title: Record and transcribe
steps.detail: Auto-record and transcribe the meeting. For Chinese meetings, domestic tools like Tongyi Tingwu transcribe more accurately. Confirm recording consent — that's the compliance baseline.
steps.tips: Skim the transcript first and fix mis-transcribed names/jargon so they don't pollute the summary.

steps.title: AI summary
steps.detail: Feed the transcript to an LLM for a structured summary: meeting goal, key discussions, decisions. Give it an output template (goal / discussion / decisions / todos) for consistent format.
steps.tips: Provide a 'notes template' as a few-shot example so output archives consistently.

steps.title: Extract action items
steps.detail: Have the model pull every action item from the transcript: what was decided, who owns it, deadline. Action items are the most valuable part of meeting notes.
steps.tips: Ask for 'owner + task + due' triples so you can import them straight into a task tool.

steps.title: Archive and distribute
steps.detail: Archive the summary plus the raw transcript in the knowledge base with date, attendees and related docs; auto-share to attendees and sync tasks to calendar/board.
steps.tips: Keep a link to the raw transcript so people can check details without replaying the whole call.

steps.title: Follow up and review
steps.detail: Check last round's action items at the start of the next meeting and do a short review; escalate anything that keeps slipping.
steps.tips: Make action items a fixed opener in your meeting template — clear old debts first, then new business.

pitfalls.title: Compliance and privacy
pitfalls.detail: Recording and transcription need attendee consent; be cautious with cloud transcription for confidential meetings.

pitfalls.title: Speaker misattribution
pitfalls.detail: Multi-speaker meetings often mislabel who said what; manually confirm 'who said what' for key decisions.

pitfalls.title: Missed action items
pitfalls.detail: AI can miss implicit commitments; walk through an 'owner + task + due' list line by line.

pitfalls.title: Over-compression loses context
pitfalls.detail: Too-tight summaries drop discussion background; keep the raw transcript link for reference.
